title: service-knowledge: each source's sync state is one durable record, the same on every node — last build, pending and failed syncs — listed in Setup, and the reconcile clears the failures it repaired
body:
repo:objectstack#5 · os-bill · session_01Utp6Cb4BAjgQ43tqy1DvVJ

Filing gate: ③ maintainer-directed (topic child). Source: topic #37000; maintainer 2026-11-27 00:12Z 「用 fable评审后拆卡，你只负责当前任务，后续任务通过信箱交接给 objectstack #1」. Reviewed by an independent Fable pass before filing (the epic's phase 4 row "sync-failure counts per source", widened to the phase's stated business result, 「管理员能看到同步状态」). Drafted on option B of the question under "Decision needed"; the What section is rewritten if the ruling is A.
Grading: area:ai · domain:server · Feature · p2 (topic) · reach: administrators of every deployment that holds a knowledge source; wrong answers today on any deployment with more than one node or after any restart · evidence: read.

## 维护者速读
- 问题：管理员现在只能用命令行看知识源的索引状态，而且「上次重建/对账的结果」只存在跑它的那台机器的内存里：多节点时看到什么靠运气，重启后就没了；同步失败只在日志里。
- 做什么：每个知识源有一条持久的状态记录：索引是否最新、上次重建或对账的时间和结果、有多少条在排队、多少条同步失败和最近的错误。管理员在设置里就能看到；每日对账补上失败的记录后把失败数清零。
- 谁受益：托管云和多节点部署的管理员；出问题时不用翻日志。
- 需要你做的：定一个问题（见下）：状态记录是否做成平台里的一张系统表并在设置里列出。

## What
Carries ADR-0161 (`docs/adr/0161-knowledge-platform-boundary-platform-owns-assembly-sync-split-record-return-knowledge-source-is-a-governed-type.md`) Execution row "row 15, and the sync-failure counts", and its Consequences line that this card changes on purpose: "A stored fingerprint and recipe hash are the only index state the service relies on. The service keeps none of its own". The fingerprint and the recipe hash stay the adapter's; what the service starts to keep is the record of its own runs and failures. It adds no adapter-contract member.

What is true on main at `579b85776`: `KnowledgeBuildRecord` is "Kept in memory, one per source, replaced by the next build: a node answers for the builds it ran, and a restarted node remembers none" (`packages/services/service-knowledge/src/knowledge-build.ts`). #37466 (PR #37578) taught the CLI to live with that: `os knowledge rebuild` infers completion from the index state where it can, and where it cannot (a rebuild of an index that is already current, which is every reconcile) it "polls until a read reaches the building node". A failed record sync is one `warn` line. The only door is `os knowledge status` and the `index_status` settings action; Setup lists nothing per source. #37309 (the Studio form) points here: "Showing index status or sync failures to an administrator: phase 4".

1. **One record per source, in a system object** the knowledge plugin registers with its manifest (as the queue plugin registers `sys_job_queue`), so it exists only where the service is mounted. The PR names it and lists it in `packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.ts`. One row per source index key (#37304's key), holding:
   - the source as callers name it, its package, adapter and object;
   - the last build: trigger (`boot`, `operator`, `reconcile`), status (the `KnowledgeBuildRecord` vocabulary), started and finished times, the counts (`discovered`, `indexed`, `skipped`, `purged`, `failed`) and the one-sentence message;
   - sync failures: how many record syncs are dead-lettered and not yet repaired, when the first and the last one failed, and the last error text, bounded in length. Never a field value of a record.
   Deployment-level state: no organization column (the #15207 rule). Rows are written by the service under the system identity and are read-only at every data door; the PR states how. The row is removed when its source is dropped (#37304's `dropSource` path). No run history is kept here: the reconcile job's history is the job service's.
2. **Writers.** `rebuildSource` writes the row when a build starts, at most every few seconds while it walks (the `BUILD_PROGRESS_LOG_INTERVAL_MS` cadence), and when it ends, for all three triggers. The queue worker (the queue card) adds one failure when a message is dead-lettered, not per attempt. A build left `running` by a node that died is closed as interrupted by the next boot or by the node that takes the lease (the precedent is `closeInterruptedSyncRuns`, `packages/services/service-automation/src/sync-run-ledger.ts`).
3. **The reconcile is the counts' reader (the epic's words).** A reconcile of a source that completes clears the failures recorded before its walk began and removes their dead letters from the queue (`purgeFailed`): the walk re-read every row, so they are repaired or no longer apply. Failures recorded during the walk stay. And the first failure of a source that had none asks for a reconcile through the reconcile card's coalesced request (the one a predicate write uses), so an outage heals without waiting for the daily run; a reconcile that itself fails asks for nothing further.
4. **Readers for people.**
   - `index_status` answers from the row, so every node answers the same; it adds the pending count, read live from the queue (`getQueueSize`), and the failure fields. The per-node caveats in `knowledge-build-actions.ts` and `packages/cli/src/commands/knowledge/status.ts` go, and `os knowledge rebuild` polls the durable record (the inference #37578 added is removed where the record makes it unnecessary; the PR states what stays for the `memory` adapter).
   - Setup lists the object: one navigation entry of type `object` beside the Knowledge settings entry, gated on `manage_platform_settings`, contributed with the service (the precedent is `nav_http_deliveries` in `packages/plugins/plugin-webhooks/src/webhook-outbox-plugin.ts`). It uses the generic object list and record page; this card adds no bespoke widget, dialog or hook. Labels enter the generated translation bundles for every locale.
5. **Texts.** `content/docs/ai/knowledge-rag.mdx` (operating a source: where to look, what each status means, what clears a failure), the `service-knowledge` README, and the ADR's Consequences sentence quoted above gets a dated note if the contract reviewer asks for one (`docs/adr/**` is the maintainer's merge).

Rulings carried (ADR-0161 K10): the count of hits removed by the permission filter is never returned to a caller, and nothing here counts hits; the record holds no record content; a key lands with its first reader in the same PR (each field above has a writer and a reader in this PR, or it is not declared).

## Acceptance
- Two nodes on one database: a rebuild started through node A is reported identically by `index_status` on node B while it runs and after it ends, including a rebuild of an index that was already current; after a restart of both, the last build is still reported.
- A build whose node is killed mid-walk reads `running` no longer than until the next boot or the next lease holder, then reads as interrupted.
- Record syncs that dead-letter raise the source's failure count by one each, with the last error and both times; a retried sync that succeeds raises nothing.
- A completed reconcile sets the count of the failures that preceded it to zero and removes their dead letters; a failure recorded during the walk survives it.
- The first failure of a source starts one reconcile after the quiet period; a hundred failures start one.
- An administrator opens Setup and sees one row per source with its state, last build and failure count; a user without `manage_platform_settings` sees no entry and is refused the rows at the data door; no door lets anyone but the service write a row.
- Removing a source removes its row. No row holds a field value of a record (a test reads the stored row after a failure whose error text was built from a provider message).
- Container run per AGENTS.md.

## Out of scope
- The queue and its retries: the queue card. The schedule and the walk: the reconcile card.
- A history of builds per source, charts, alerts or notifications on failure: not here; each returns with a reader.
- Showing status inside the Studio form of a source (#37309): that form may link to this list; it adds no status of its own.
- Hosted and Enterprise views of the same rows: cloud's (rows 13 and 14 are cloud-repo cards).

## Decision needed

### 维护者速读（待你定）
- 问题：管理员想知道「知识源同步得怎么样」，现在只能用命令行问，而且多节点时每台机器答得不一样、重启后忘光；失败只在日志里。
- 选项：A 不加存储，状态从任务队列和定时任务的记录里现算，仍只在命令行看，约一个小 PR；B 每个知识源存一条持久状态记录（一张系统表），设置里直接列出来，每台机器答得一样，约一个中等 PR。
- 推荐 B：这是这一阶段承诺的业务结果「管理员能看到同步状态」，托管云的管理员没有命令行。
- 不定会怎样：这张卡开不了工；对账和排队两张卡不受影响，照常做，只是失败仍然只在日志和队列里。

### Q1 — Where a source's sync state lives, and whether an administrator sees it in Setup

**Problem.** An administrator cannot see whether a knowledge source is in step with its data: the answer depends on which server took the question, is forgotten at restart, and never mentions failed syncs.

**Governing text.** Epic #37000, phase 4: 「业务结果：保存不再等向量服务；服务宕机后索引能自动追平；管理员能看到同步状态。」 and the row "sync-failure counts per source (row; its reader is row 15's reconcile)". ADR-0161 Consequences: "A stored fingerprint and recipe hash are the only index state the service relies on. The service keeps none of its own". `git grep -n "Kept in memory" packages/services/service-knowledge/src/knowledge-build.ts` → the build record's note. No ruling on where the state lives: `gh` search `knowledge build record durable shared nodes` → 16 hits, none on this; #37466 chose its CLI-only option to avoid editing the service while #37465 and #37304 held the file, not as a position.

**Protocol.** B adds one platform system object (no authorable key, no adapter-contract member); the PR declares what the metadata-protocol gates ask of a new system object. A adds nothing.

**Premise, re-check.** `git grep -n "a restarted node remembers none" packages/services/service-knowledge/src/knowledge-build.ts`; `git grep -n "polls until" packages/cli/src/commands/knowledge/` (the #37578 behaviour); `git grep -n "nav_http_deliveries" packages/plugins/plugin-webhooks/src/webhook-outbox-plugin.ts` (the Setup precedent B uses).

| Option | What it does | What the customer sees | Effort |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| A — derive, store nothing | `index_status` adds a pending count and a failure count read from the queue's dead letters (paged and grouped by the source named in each message) and the last reconcile from the job's run history; the build record stays in memory on the node that ran it | command line only; the last rebuild is still per node and gone at restart; counting failures after an outage means paging thousands of dead letters on every status read | `domain:server` · 1 PR · no measured precedent (the nearest, PR #37578 for #37466, +306/−51, is the CLI workaround this option keeps) |
| B — one durable record per source, listed in Setup | a system object the service writes (last build, failure count and last error), read by `index_status`, by the reconcile and by a generic list page in Setup | the same answer from every node and after a restart; an administrator opens Setup → Knowledge and sees each source's state and failures; no command line needed | `domain:server` · 1 PR, medium · precedent PR #32385 (`sys_sync_run`, the sync-in run ledger with its writer, +1612/−91, 21 files); the Setup entry has a precedent with no separate line count (`nav_http_deliveries`) |

Business meaning: A is "ask the night shift what happened, and hope the same person is on duty"; B is "there is a logbook at the door".

os-decision-facets
① Long-term: B makes the status one fact with one home, and removes the per-node special case and the CLI inference added for it; A keeps two partial truths (a node's memory, and counts re-derived from another service's tables) and one more special case each time a door reads them.
② Business pull: today one application (BrightRule) on one node, where A's gaps rarely show; the hosted mount (the epic's row 14) is multi-node and its administrators have no command line, and a provider outage on any deployment leaves failures nobody is shown.
③ AI-error: not an authoring surface; on the operator side A's failure is silent (a node with no record answers as if nothing ran), B's is visible (a `failed` row with its message).
④ Startup scope: B declares one system object and one Setup entry, kept for good; A declares nothing.
Prior rulings read: `knowledge build record durable shared nodes` → 16 hits (none on this point; #37466 closed with the CLI-only option) · `"os knowledge status"` → 14 hits (#37466, #37099) · ADR-0161 Consequences (quoted above); ADR-0153 D7 (`sys_sync_run`, the precedent); thread: none.

**Recommendation: B.** End state: two years on, every knowledge source has a status an administrator reads where sources are configured, as mainstream platforms show it (Salesforce Data Cloud's search-index status, Elasticsearch's index and ingest stats, Algolia's index operations log) and as this platform already does for sync-in (`sys_sync_run`) and webhook deliveries (`sys_http_delivery`). Confidence gap: whether hosted administrators should see the raw system-object list or a view cloud builds on the same rows; B as written gives the generic list and leaves the hosted view to cloud. A not taken: it leaves the phase's stated result unmet on any deployment with two nodes or a restart.
Self-check: only ① gives B; ②③④ flip it: no (④ weighs against, not enough to flip; ② only moves timing, and the card already sits last in the phase).
After the ruling: B — the card stands as written and waits for its two blockers. A — the What section shrinks to item 3 (failures read from the queue) and the `index_status` half of item 4; items 1 and 2 and the Setup entry are dropped, and the title is rewritten.

Blocked-by: #37734 (the reconcile card: the counts' reader and the coalesced request), #37735 (the queue card: the dead letters being counted), #37304 (the index key and the `dropSource` path). Numbers of the two sibling cards are filled in at filing.
Coordinates with #37309 (its out-of-scope line points here), #37104 (same settings contribution file).
Parent: #37000. Reader: `domain:server` lane (`packages/services/service-knowledge`, `packages/cli/src/commands/knowledge`; the object's labels in `packages/platform-objects` translations).
Dedupe: `knowledge sync failure count` 115 (open: #37309, #37304, #37000, #32062 — sync-in, another subsystem; none counts knowledge sync failures) · `"os knowledge status"` 14 (open: #37104, #37636 — unrelated; closed: #37466 — the CLI workaround this card replaces) · `knowledge index status Setup administrator sync` 18 (open: #37304 and seat posts; none lists status in Setup) · `sys_knowledge` 0.
